Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Prime–rest–rechallenge with windowed AP-1 degradation (the "inward eye" recall test)
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (serum, TGF-β, wounding, or drug), allow full return to baseline transcriptome, then restimulate days later and quantify whether the secondary response is faster, larger, or qualitatively different — the signature of recall. Use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron on FOS/JUN to delete AP-1 selectively during the priming window, the quiescent storage window, or the recall window, which dissociates AP-1's role as the writer, the maintainer, or merely the reader of the memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage tracing of primed state through quiescence
ideas.description: Combine a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter with expressed lineage barcodes (e.g., Watermelon/CellTag-style) so that individual primed cells and their descendants can be re-identified at rechallenge and profiled by scRNA-seq. This distinguishes true per-cell memory from a population-level artifact in which a pre-existing responsive subpopulation is simply selected or expanded, and it measures what fraction of cells actually retain the state.

ideas.title: Division-coupled decay and mitotic bookmarking assay
ideas.description: Prime cells, then use CFSE dilution or a FUCCI/division-counting reporter to sort descendants by number of divisions completed, and measure memory half-life in units of cell divisions rather than hours. In parallel, perform mitotic-chromosome CUT&RUN and live imaging of tagged FOS/JUN in mitosis to test whether AP-1 remains bound to memory enhancers during mitosis, the physical mechanism that would allow the state to be copied to daughters.

ideas.title: Dimer-composition code at memory enhancers
ideas.description: Apply sequential/dual CUT&RUN (or CUT&Tag with antibodies against FOS, FOSB, FRA1, FRA2, JUN, JUNB, JUND) plus quantitative IP–mass spectrometry across the priming, resting, and recall phases to determine whether the persistent feature is a specific long-lived dimer, such as a FOSB/ΔFOSB-containing complex, rather than total AP-1 occupancy. Then swap dimer identity by targeted knock-in or degron and test whether memory duration tracks the dimer's protein half-life.

ideas.title: Single-molecule binding kinetics and optogenetic pulse decoding
ideas.description: Use HaloTag single-molecule tracking and FRAP on endogenous JUN/FOS to measure residence time, bound fraction, and search kinetics at primed versus naive enhancers, testing whether memory is stored in binding dynamics even when ChIP-level occupancy appears unchanged. Pair this with optogenetic or chemically dimerizable AP-1 to deliver defined pulse amplitudes, durations, and frequencies, identifying the minimal dynamic input that installs a lasting chromatin-accessibility change measured by time-resolved ATAC-seq.
